newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds close up despite small rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds close up despite small rate cut.

text.p: Israel's bonds closed up on Wednesday despite the disappointment caused by the small interest rate cut on Tuesday, traders said. Arab violence over Israel's opening of a tunnel under the Old City of Jerusalem did not affect the market.
* Consumer price index (CPI) linked government bonds: +0.2 pct to 166.73
* Dollar linked government bonds: -0.2 pct to 161.81
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for 4 years): unchanged at 164.52
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: unchanged at 156.68

"There was strong demand for CPI-linked bonds, trading in unlinked bonds was mixed and there was surplus supply for dollar linked bonds," said Adam Reuter, managing director of Financial Immunities, a financial and economic consultancy.
"All in all the market reacted negatively to the low interest rate cut and the market would have risen much more had the cut been greater," he said.
On Tuesday the central bank said it was lowering its key lending rate for October by 0.3 percent to an annualised 15.5 percent.

"The bond market has been going up for the past few weeks manily because there are fewer redemptions from provident funds and because the central bank's security net for the bonds has helped calm the market," he said.

Israel's low stock and bond prices have affected the performance of provident funds, long term savings funds with special tax benefits, triggering public redemptions. Provident funds, major investors in the bond market, have been dumping bonds to meet the massive redemptions. To stop the falling prices in the bond market, the central bank has intervened in the bond market by buying government bonds. Most of the falling prices were in CPI-linked bonds.

Danny Alt, of Nassua Trading and Investment in Securities Ltd, said the rise in prices in CPI-linked bonds was due mainly to lower provident fund redemptions and to the fact that the Treasury had practically stopped issuing CPI-linked bonds and was issuing mainly unlinked bonds.
"The central bank issued unlinked bonds today worth 500 million shekels for the Treasury. Despite the big issue the bonds are performing well," he said.
Both Reuter and Alt said that political unrest in Jerusalem, over the opening of a tunnel in the Old City, had not affected trading.

Note: The Bank of Israel short term Makam bills are debt certificates issued for periods ranging from three months to one year. The bills are zero-coupon, unlinked short-term notes. The Bank of Israel issues the certificates which are used as a monetary instrument, to absorb money from the public.
